title: Smart Data Models - TM Forum Open APIs - ResourceCatalog
description: The root entity for resource catalog management. A resource catalog is a group of resource specifications made available through resource candidates that an organization provides to the consumers (internal consumers like its employees or B2B customers or B2C customers). (TM Forum TMF634 Resource Catalog Management 5.0.0, OpenAPI component ResourceCatalog; attribute names kept verbatim except the NGSI-LD reserved terms / JSON-LD keywords renamed with a tmf prefix (id, @type, @baseType, @schemaLocation, ...); deprecated attributes left out.)

type.description: Property. NGSI-LD Entity type. It must be equal to 'ResourceCatalog'

lifecycleStatus.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF634_ResourceCatalog/blob/v5.0.0/TMF634-Resource_Catalog_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Catalog/properties/lifecycleStatus'. Used to indicate the current lifecycle status

category.description: Relationship. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF634_ResourceCatalog/blob/v5.0.0/TMF634-Resource_Catalog_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/ResourceCatalog/properties/category'. List of root categories contained in this catalog. In TMF this is an array of ResourceCategoryRef objects; here the NGSI-LD ids of the referenced ResourceCategory entities (urn:ngsi-ld:ResourceCategory:<tmf id>). Inline values and reference metadata (href, name, @referredType) are not kept.

externalIdentifier.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF634_ResourceCatalog/blob/v5.0.0/TMF634-Resource_Catalog_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/ResourceCatalog/properties/externalIdentifier'. An identification of an entity that is owned by or originates in a software system different from the current system, for example a ProductOrder handed off from a commerce platform into an order handling system. The structure identifies the system itself, the nature of the entity within the system (e.g. class name) and the unique ID of the entity within the system. It is anticipated that multiple external IDs can be held for a single entity, e.g. if the entity passed through multiple systems on the way to the current system. In this case the consumer is expected to sequence the IDs in the array in reverse order of provenance, i.e. most recent system first in the list.
